newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq paper predicts tension with U.N. inspectors.
newsitem.headline: Iraq paper predicts tension with U.N. inspectors.

text.p: Iraq's most influential newspaper on Tuesday predicted rising tension between Iraq and U.N. arms inspectors after a U.N. resolution threatening Baghdad with further sanctions if it obstructed inspections.

"The coming months will see an escalation of provocative acts and attempts to encroach upon Iraq's sovereignty and security," said Babel, the newspaper owned by President Saddam Hussein's eldest son, Uday.
The U.N. Security Council on Saturday unanimously warned Iraq it would face further sanctions if it did not allow U.N. arms inspectors to search sensitive sites.

Rolf Ekeus, chairman of the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) in charge of dismantling Iraq's prohibited weapons, complained to the Council that Baghdad had this month blocked his arms inspectors from three sites.
The Iraqi leadership rejected the resolution, saying it was unjustified. It also accused the United States of being behind the resolution.
"Iraq will be pressed to respond to these provocations...then America will issue a new resolution postponing the lifting of sanctions and impose new sanctions on Iraq," Babel said.
UNSCOM must certify that Iraq has no weapons of mass destruction before the United Nations will lift curbs on its oil exports imposed after Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The U.N. has allowed Baghdad since December to sell $2 billion worth of oil to buy urgently needed goods.
Babel also called on China, Russia and France, which are adopting a less tough stance toward Iraq, to set up an arbitration committee between Iraq and UNSCOM.

"There should be an arbitration committee between Iraq and the Special Commission to examine the inspectors' accusations and to listen to Iraq's opinion...France, China and Russia should follow such a request," the paper said.
